subject: Request: Additional sandbox credits for 48h latency/throughput POC
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmedata.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@acmedata.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sandbox credit request for 48h latency/throughput POC

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the runtime looked very promising. We want to run a 48-hour POC to validate latency SLOs at 6k concurrent requests/min and characterize per-token cost under sustained load. Our engineering team will run two full soak windows (12h each) plus a 24h mixed traffic run.

Can Redwood provision a short-term credit allowance and a temporary bump in capacity for this POC? Rough ask: equivalent of $8k in credits (or ~200k tokens) and a 48h capacity window with autoscale limits raised to support the peak.

I've attached our POC run plan (acme_poc_run_plan.xlsx) and a short outline of test scenarios. Procurement may require a simple credit agreement or confirmation email that this is a promotional, non-recurring grant. Copying procurement (procurement@acmedata.com) and Elena from infra.

Timing: we hope to run the soak next Tuesday (May 12) but can be flexible if you need lead time.

Appreciate any options and next steps — happy to jump on a quick call.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Data
[Attachment: acme_poc_run_plan.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmedata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sandbox credit request for 48h latency/throughput POC

Samir — thanks for the plan and clear numbers. Really helpful. We can absolutely support a short burst and promotional credit for a POC like this, but I need to confirm a couple of operational items with our CS and infra teams:

- Exact concurrency pattern (sustained vs spikes) and warmup window
- Whether KV/prefix caching will be used (affects cost)
- If you need any dedicated routing/region pinning for the run

Monica/Stephanie — can you review the attached plan and advise on the capacity and cost delta? If ops can support the 48h burst at the asked throughput, I can approve a one-time sponsorship for the promotional credit.

Samir — provisional next steps from my side:
1) Monica to confirm capacity and a rough cost estimate by EOD tomorrow.
2) If estimate is within ~$10k, I will approve the sponsorship and ask finance/procurement to sign a simple credit agreement (we use a short form — see redwood_credit_agreement_v1.pdf).
3) We'll provision the credit and enable the capacity window; procurement can accept the one-time grant terms.

Proposed small ask: if Acme can share a short acceptance note (email) from procurement acknowledging the promotional nature, that smooths the internal approval.

Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_credit_agreement_v1.pdf]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmedata.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sandbox credit request for 48h latency/throughput POC

Karthik / Stephanie — reviewed Acme's run plan. Key points:

- Traffic profile: 6k concurrent req/min steady for two 12h windows, then a mixed 24h with 70% GETs and 30% generate calls.
- Estimated token consumption: ~180k-220k tokens depending on payload and caching.
- Ops impact: we can enable a temporary autoscale burst for the requested 48h window; no dedicated hardware required but we'll raise per-instance concurrency caps and monitor closely.

Cost estimate (rough): promotional credit equivalent to $7.5k should cover typical variability and give a safety buffer (~200k tokens). I've attached a quick calc (acme_cost_estimate.csv).

Ask to Karthik: please approve a one-time promotional credit of $7.5k (label: RDW-PROMO-ACME-0047) and confirm start/end windows. If approved, I'll coordinate with infra to set capacity and with finance to issue the credit. We'll also attach the short-form agreement (redwood_credit_agreement_v1.pdf) and ask Acme procurement to confirm via email.

Samir — can procurement send a confirmation email approving the grant terms (one-time promotional credit) once we share the agreement? That will be enough for our finance team to proceed.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme_cost_estimate.csv]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmedata.com>, procurement@acmedata.com
Date: Sat, 8 May 2026 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sandbox credit request for 48h latency/throughput POC

Approved.

Monica — please provision a one-time promotional credit RDW-PROMO-ACME-0047 equal to $7.5k (approx. 200k tokens) and set an expiry of 2026-06-06. Enable the 48h capacity window starting May 12 00:00 PT (unless Acme confirms alternate start) with autoscale caps raised to support the stated peak. Stephanie — coordinate the temporary capacity change and provide a monitoring hook to our on-call infra during the soak.

Marissa — loop in finance to prepare the short-form credit agreement; procurement@acmedata.com has been CC'd — Samir, please reply to confirm acceptance of the promotional grant terms so finance has an audit trail. Also updating HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567 (deal RDW-ACME-2026-0047).

Thanks all — let's keep the run quiet and closely monitored so we can collect clean latency data.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Action: provision credit RDW-PROMO-ACME-0047; attach redwood_credit_agreement_v1.pdf to outbound to procurement]
